Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

LONDON, England (CNN) -- Britain's Prince William is starting a two-month attachment with the Royal Navy on Monday, part of the future king's continued experience with various branches of the military, the Ministry of Defense said Saturday. Prince William and his father, Prince Charles, at his graduation from the Royal Air Force in April. William, 25, will spend the first part of his attachment on a basic sea safety course training in sea survival, firefighting and ship damage repair, according to the ministry. If William passes the course, as expected, he will join the HMS Iron Duke in the Caribbean, the department said. The ship's function is to support overseas British territories in the event of a hurricane and to carry out counter-narcotic operations. The prince, who will be called Sub Lieutenant Wales in the Navy, is expected to spend time aboard a frigate, a mine hunter, a submarine and helicopters during his attachment, which ends August 1, the Ministry of Defense said. William completed a four-month attachment with the Royal Air Force this year and received his pilot's wings upon graduating in April. He learned to fly three different aircraft during the attachment and is known as Flying Officer Wales within the RAF. William is also a second lieutenant in the British Army, where he serves in the Blues and Royals regiment of the Household Cavalry. The attachments are designed to provide the prince with military experience for when he becomes head of the armed forces as king. "When he becomes king, he needs to know his armed forces -- instinctively be very familiar with them -- and so he is doing this visit to the Royal Navy," said Rear Adm. Bob Cooling, the assistant chief of naval staff. William's father, Prince Charles, had a five-year career in the navy in the 1970s. Charles served on the guided missile destroyer HMS Norfolk and two frigates before qualifying as a helicopter pilot and joining a naval air squadron that operated from the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes. Prince Charles spent his last nine months in the navy in 1976 in command of the coastal minehunter HMS Bronington. William's uncle Prince Andrew served 22 years in the Royal Navy as a helicopter pilot, seeing active service during the Falklands War between Britain and Argentina in 1982. Queen Elizabeth II's husband, Prince Philip, William's grandfather, spent more than 13 years in the Royal Navy. He saw active service throughout World War II and was in Tokyo Harbor when Japan surrendered.

Prince William was scheduled to begin a two-month attachment with the Royal Navy in June 2008, completing a programme designed to give the future king experience across all three branches of Britain’s armed forces.

Serving as **Sub-Lieutenant Wales**, he was to start at Britannia Royal Naval College in Dartmouth with instruction in navigation, seamanship, firefighting and damage control. **Prince William Follows Family Tradition at Sea**  
*July 2008*

Prince William has added a Royal Navy posting to his growing military résumé, serving under the name **Sub Lieutenant Wales** during a short attachment designed to give him experience of Britain’s three armed services.

The prince, who graduated from the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst in 2006 and was commissioned into the Household Cavalry’s Blues and Royals, began his naval attachment this summer. After introductory training, he joined the frigate **HMS *Iron Duke*** for operations in the Caribbean and North Atlantic.

As Sub Lieutenant Wales, William has taken part in the everyday work of a junior naval officer, including watchkeeping and navigation duties. HMS *Iron Duke* has also been involved in counter-narcotics patrols, disaster-relief readiness and visits intended to strengthen Britain’s ties with Caribbean territories.

The attachment is not expected to mark a permanent transfer from the Army. Rather, it forms part of William’s broader preparation for his future public role by giving him first-hand knowledge of the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as well as the Army. Earlier in 2008, he completed an RAF attachment and learned to fly under military instruction.

William’s spell at sea continues a strong naval tradition within the Royal Family.

### The Prince of Wales

William’s father, **Prince Charles**, served in the Royal Navy during the 1970s after undertaking flying training with the Royal Air Force. He qualified as a helicopter pilot and served aboard several warships, including the guided-missile destroyer **HMS *Norfolk*** and the frigates **HMS *Minerva*** and **HMS *Jupiter***.

In 1976, Charles took command of the coastal minehunter **HMS *Bronington***, his final appointment in regular naval service. His command of the vessel remains one of the most significant operational posts held by a modern heir to the throne.

### The Duke of York

Prince William’s uncle, **Prince Andrew, Duke of York**, had the longest recent full-time naval career among the Queen’s sons. He entered the Royal Navy in 1979 and trained as a helicopter pilot.

During the 1982 Falklands conflict, Andrew served aboard the aircraft carrier **HMS *Invincible***, flying Sea King helicopters on missions that included anti-submarine patrols, casualty evacuation and other operational duties. He later commanded the minehunter **HMS *Cottesmore*** and held a number of staff appointments before leaving active service in 2001 after more than two decades in uniform.

### The Duke of Edinburgh

William’s grandfather, **Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh**, also had a distinguished naval career. He entered the Royal Navy as a cadet in 1939 and served throughout the Second World War in the Mediterranean, Indian Ocean and Pacific.

His wartime service included duty aboard the battleship **HMS *Valiant***, where he was mentioned in despatches following the Battle of Cape Matapan in 1941. He later served as first lieutenant of the destroyer **HMS *Whelp*** in the Pacific and was present in Tokyo Bay when Japan formally surrendered in 1945.

Philip continued his career after the war, commanding the frigate **HMS *Magpie***. He gave up active naval service in 1951 as the then Princess Elizabeth’s royal responsibilities increased, having reached the rank of commander. He has since held several honorary senior service ranks, including Admiral of the Fleet.

Prince William’s time as Sub Lieutenant Wales may be comparatively brief, but it places him firmly within a family tradition extending from wartime destroyers and aircraft carriers to modern patrols in the Caribbean.
